falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/GameStateStore.cs:59; remove the IsResourceEvent(e.eventType) gate -> this cell stays green because the two TechResearched keys differ ('basicRocketry'/'stability'), so the key gate still keeps 2 events
what_it_asserts: Two non-resource events at the same UT are never coalesced.
why_weak: The differing keys over-determine the split; no cell feeds two same-type, same-key, same-tag non-resource events within the window, so dropping the resource-type gate would silently coalesce (drop) career events such as TechResearched/PartPurchased and the suite stays green.
proposed_action: Use the same key ('basicRocketry') on both TechResearched events at ut 100.0; the cell then reds if the IsResourceEvent gate disappears.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/SuppressionGuard.cs:39; deleting the two flag assignments in ResourcesAndReplay -> this cell stays green, because the flags are only read before and after PatchAll
what_it_asserts: That GameStateRecorder.SuppressResourceEvents and IsReplayingActions are false before and after PatchAll, plus the 'PatchAll complete' log.
why_weak: The name's Sets half is unverified: no assertion runs inside the using scope, so a PatchAll that never suppressed resource/replay events (or dropped the guard at KspStatePatcher.cs:72 entirely) still greens. Only a regression that leaves the flags set can red it.
proposed_action: Rename to PatchAll_RestoresSuppressionFlags and add a direct SuppressionGuard.ResourcesAndReplay test asserting both flags true while the scope is live; the set-at-entry half is otherwise pinned only by the using site at KspStatePatcher.cs:72.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/GameActions/ContractsModule.cs:509; set terminalContractActions[id]/terminalContractOutcomes[id] only when the key is absent (first-wins) -> this cell stays green, since c1/c2/c3/c4 each record exactly one terminal action
what_it_asserts: The terminal-action and terminal-outcome maps carry Completed/Failed/Cancelled for c1/c2/c3 and DeadlineExpired for c4 (reached through CheckDeadlines).
why_weak: Every contract id receives exactly one terminal action, so the 'latest outcome wins' behavior the name claims is never discriminated: a first-wins guard on the two maps passes unchanged. Those maps drive KspStatePatcher's tombstone discrimination (ContractsModule.cs:50-59).
proposed_action: Add a cell that fails then cancels one id with no intervening Accept (a re-accept clears both maps at ContractsModule.cs:378-379) and assert the maps end on ContractCancel/Cancelled.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/EffectiveState.cs:1065; the sealed-tip filter that SealedSlot_NotMember pins would exclude a genuinely Immutable row, so flipping the fixture to MergeState.Immutable -> red on the current Assert.Single
what_it_asserts: a Destroyed recording under a RewindPoint is an Unfinished Flights member
why_weak: the name, the doc comment and the regression it claims all say Immutable, but the fixture passes MergeState.CommittedProvisional; that makes it an exact duplicate of CommittedProvisionalDestroyedUnderRP_IsMember (same ids, same rp, same assertions) and leaves the Immutable+Destroyed-under-RP case with no coverage at all
proposed_action: delete this test as the duplicate it is and add a real Immutable+Destroyed-under-RP case asserting the sealedTipClosed exclusion, or rename it to match the CommittedProvisional fixture it actually uses

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/FlightRecorder.cs:9931-9936; delete the elapsedSeconds>0 guard -> this test stays green
what_it_asserts: that DiagnosticsState.activeGrowthRate.pointsPerSecond and eventsPerSecond equal the 0.0 the test itself assigned, and that FormatReport emits no NaN
why_weak: the zero-elapsed division guard is in FlightRecorder growth-rate computation and is never invoked; the struct is hand-filled, so the named regression cannot red it
proposed_action: call the FlightRecorder growth-rate computation with elapsedSeconds=0, or extract it to a pure internal static helper, and assert the result is 0.0 and not NaN

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/Logistics/RouteOrchestrator.cs:4449; stub RouteKscFundsCost to 0f on the RouteCargoDelivered row -> still green, the asserted row is authored by InstallFakeDeliveryApplier
what_it_asserts: delivered.RouteKscFundsCost == 555f on a career KSC-origin loop crossing.
why_weak: DeliveryApplierForTesting replaces production ApplyDelivery; the fake computes the funds value from its own argument, so no production funds code is exercised.
proposed_action: Assert the funds cost on the production-emitted RouteCargoDebited row (EmitDispatchDebit:3607) instead, or cover ApplyDelivery funds in a test that leaves the delivery seam null.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/Logistics/RouteRunCostCalculator.cs:143; drop the treeRecordingIds.Contains check -> red; no edit that rescopes the sum to Route.RecordingIds exists at this SUT
what_it_asserts: A recovery row whose id is a tree member but not a route member is summed (5400, count 1), plus a self-assertion that the id is absent from route.RecordingIds.
why_weak: SumRecoveredCredits takes the scope set as a parameter and reads route only for logging (line 110), so the G1 rescoping regression the comment names cannot be introduced here; the real guard is ResolveTreeRecordingIds.
proposed_action: Retitle and recomment to state it pins parameter-scoped membership, or move the G1 claim onto a Compute() level test that builds the scope through ResolveTreeRecordingIds.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/MapRender/CrossMemberSeamStitcher.cs:188; halve the returned difference -> test stays GREEN; it reds only after the tolerance is tightened
why_weak: The third argument 4f binds xUnit 2.4.2's float tolerance overload (not the int precision overload, which a float literal cannot bind), so the accepted window is +/-4.0 around 3 and 4. Any x in [-1,7] and y in [0,8] passes, including a zero, halved or sign-flipped y. This is the only test of the tangent the G1 seam predicate consumes.
proposed_action: Use a real tolerance, e.g. Assert.Equal(3f, t.x, 1e-4f) and Assert.Equal(4f, t.y, 1e-4f), and add the z component.

falsifiability: falsifiability: Source/Parsek/MapRender/CrossMemberSeamStitcher.cs:290; drive DriveUT from the raw liveUT instead of the re-anchored head -> red on the expectedHead assert; the sa.DriveUT==sb.DriveUT assert can never red
what_it_asserts: That two identical TryStitchDescentSeam calls both return DriveUT == recordedDeorbitUT + (liveUT - triggerUT).
why_weak: The comment claims the ordering contract is proven by passing a deliberately-wrong sampleUT, but TryStitchDescentSeam has no sampleUT parameter and the two calls use identical arguments, so the independence assertion is a tautology. What remains is the DriveUT value, already asserted by Stitch_TriggeredDescentMember_PromotesVisibleTracedPathDescent, leaving the compose-after-remap ordering contract untested.
proposed_action: Either exercise the ordering through the caller that supplies the post-remap sample (ChainSampler.Sample) with a perturbed remap, or drop the second call and the sampleUT wording so the test only claims what it proves.
